questions.q: Choose the correct form: “Many a student ____ failed in this examination.”
questions.why: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “The professor, who ____ at this university since 1998, retires next month.”
questions.why: 'Since 1998' up to now requires the present perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive form: “He wants someone to repair the clinic roof.”
opts: He wants the clinic roof being repaired.
He wants the clinic roof to repair.
He wants the clinic roof to be repaired.
He is wanted the clinic roof repaired.
questions.why: The passive infinitive is 'to be + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “He is averse ____ taking risks.”

questions.why: The only English word ending in -sede (with no other -cede form). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Their report, however, was rejected by the board.
Q. A team of researchers spent two years collecting data.
R. They claimed their results proved the drug’s safety.
S. The sample size, the board felt, was too small.
questions.why: Claim, then 'however' rejection, then the reason for it. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Which sentence contains an adjective clause?
opts: I know the place where he lives.
questions.why: In the key, 'where he lives' qualifies the noun 'place'; in the others the clause is a noun or adverb clause. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “munificent”:
questions.why: 'Munificent' means very generous; 'parsimonious' means extremely stingy. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “He failed the exam, ____ surprised nobody.”
questions.why: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'that' cannot follow a comma. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct version: “Walking down the corridor, the lights suddenly went off.”
opts: As I was walking down the corridor, the lights suddenly went off.
While walking down the corridor, the lights suddenly went off.
Walking down the corridor, suddenly the lights went off.
The lights suddenly went off, walking down the corridor.
questions.why: The participial phrase dangles; only the clause with its own subject is correct. GPSC-style practice item.
